---
title: Rules
---

Rules report problems in a BibTeX project.
Run `biblint check` to use the configured rule set, `biblint rule` to list every rule, or `biblint rule <name>` to read one rule's summary and fix status.

## Rule reference

The default set focuses on syntax and structural problems.
Formatting, citekey style, and project-wide duplicate comparisons are opt-in:

| Rule | Default | Severity | Fix  | Purpose                                                     |
| ---- | :-----: | :------: | :--: | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `syntax_error`  | yes     | error    | none | BibTeX syntax is incomplete or unbalanced.                  |
| `formatting`  | no      | note     | safe | The file would be reformatted by biblint.                   |
| `missing_key`  | yes     | warning  | none | An entry has no citation key.                               |
| `key_format`  | no      | warning  | none | An existing key differs from the configured key formula.    |
| `duplicate_key`  | yes     | warning  | none | A citation key is used more than once.                      |
| `duplicate_doi`  | no      | warning  | none | Two entries share a DOI.                                    |
| `duplicate_citation`  | no      | warning  | none | Two entries share a normalized citation fingerprint.        |
| `duplicate_abstract` | no      | warning  | none | Two entries share an abstract fingerprint.                  |
| `duplicate_field` | yes     | warning  | none | An entry repeats a field name.                              |
| `empty_field` | yes     | warning  | none | A field has no value.                                       |
| `nonstandard_name_separator` | yes     | warning  | none | A creator list uses `with` or a comma before `and`.            |
| `invalid_suppression` | yes     | warning  | none | A suppression comment is malformed, misplaced, or obsolete. |
| `unsupported_escape` | yes     | note     | none | A character has no built-in LaTeX escape.                   |
| `unsupported_construct` | yes     | note     | none | Source was preserved because it could not be structured.    |

Warnings produce exit status `1`; errors produce exit status `2`.
Notes are still diagnostics and therefore also make `check` return `1` when they are reported.
See [Configuration](configuration.qmd) for changing the selection.

## Inline suppressions

Place a standalone `% biblint-ignore` comment immediately before the entry it belongs to.
Name one or more rules, and optionally add a reason after `:`:

```bibtex
% biblint-ignore nonstandard_name_separator duplicate_field: legacy source
@book{garfinkel1997,
  author = {Simson Garfinkel with Gene Spafford},
}
```

The directive applies only to the next BibTeX entry.
Multiple directives before one entry are combined.
Suppressions cannot hide syntax errors or whole-file formatting diagnostics, and malformed, misplaced, or unused directives are reported by `invalid_suppression`.

`nonstandard_name_separator` checks `author`, `editor`, `translator`, and `collaborator` values.
It only examines text outside nested braces and does not rewrite values.
A literal phrase such as `Smith with Jones` can be protected by bracing the intended literal name.

## Select rules

Use `select` to replace the default set, `extend-select` to add to it, and `ignore` to disable a rule regardless of how it was selected:

```toml
[lint]
select = ["duplicate_key"]
extend-select = ["key_format", "duplicate_doi"]
ignore = ["unsupported_escape"]
```

Use `all` as a wildcard.
Per-file exceptions use the same rule names:

```toml
[lint.per-file-ignores]
"generated/**" = ["formatting", "unsupported_construct"]
```

Formatting is not enabled for `check` by default because it is a mechanical rewrite rather than a content diagnostic.
For a one-off formatting check, add `--format` to the command.
For a formatting-only gate, use `biblint format <path> --check`.

## Project-level checks

When checking a directory or multiple files, biblint also detects duplicates across files.
DOI, citation, and abstract comparisons are disabled by default; enable only the comparisons useful for the project.
A single explicit file gets single-file checks and does not create a project-wide comparison.

## Key-format checks

`key_format` is disabled by default because changing a citation key can break references elsewhere.
Enable it explicitly to report suggestions:

```toml
[lint]
extend-select = ["key_format"]

[lint.key-format]
style = "better-bibtex"
```

The rule reports a suggestion but does not rename keys automatically.
See [Citekey generation](key-generation.md) to configure the formula and, if desired, apply generated keys through the formatter.
